audits.title: Piloting laboratory quality system management in six health facilities in Nigeria.
audits.setting: Six health facility laboratories in five states

cycle1.result: Baseline: two labs 1-star, four 0-star; internal audit 4%, occurrence management 15%.

audits.intervention: Advocacy, capacity building, mentorship and quality improvement projects.

cycle2.result: Exit: four labs 4-star, one 3-star, one 2-star; internal audit 76%, occurrence management 81%.

audits.other_findings: One laboratory dropped a star between follow-up and exit audits.
audits.citation: Mbah H, Ojo E, Ameh J, Musuluma H, Negedu-Momoh OR, Jegede F, et al.. Piloting laboratory quality system management in six health facilities in Nigeria. PLoS One. 2014;9(12):e116185. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0116185. PMID: 25542022.

audits.title: Laboratory system strengthening and quality improvement in Ethiopia.
audits.standard: WHO AFRO SLIPTA checklist star rating
audits.setting: 45 Ethiopian laboratories in two SLMTA cohorts

cycle1.result: Baseline audit compliance (figures not legible in abstract).

audits.intervention: SLMTA training, improvement projects and supportive supervision.

cycle2.result: At exit, 61% of cohort I and 48% of cohort II laboratories increased their star rating.

audits.other_findings: Challenges: poor awareness, lack of harmonisation and absence of a quality manual.
audits.citation: Hiwotu TM, Ayana G, Mulugeta A, Kassa GB, Kebede Y, Fonjungo PN, et al.. Laboratory system strengthening and quality improvement in Ethiopia. Afr J Lab Med. 2014;3(2):228. doi:10.4102/ajlm.v3i2.228. PMID: 26753129.

audits.title: Implementing Laboratory Quality Management Systems in Mozambique: The Becton Dickinson-US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief Public-Private Partnership Initiative.
audits.standard: WHO AFRO SLIPTA checklist (13 quality system essentials)
audits.intervention: SLMTA curriculum, training and mentorship of local auditors and managers.

cycle2.result: Final audits showed improvement across the 13 quality system essentials compared with baseline (figures not given).

audits.other_findings: 18 auditors qualified and 28 managers or quality officers trained.
audits.citation: Skaggs B, Pinto I, Masamha J, Turgeon D, Gudo ES. audits.title: The impact of SLMTA in improving laboratory quality systems in the Caribbean Region.
audits.setting: Five national reference laboratories in four Caribbean countries
audits.intervention: SLMTA training, improvement projects, mentorship and implementation plans after each audit.

cycle2.result: One laboratory reached four stars, two three stars and two two stars.

audits.other_findings: Audits at baseline, 6, 12 and 18 months; over 100 SOPs developed per laboratory.
audits.citation: Guevara G, Gordon F, Irving Y, Whyms I, Parris K, Beckles S, et al.. The impact of SLMTA in improving laboratory quality systems in the Caribbean Region. Afr J Lab Med. 2014;3(2):199. doi:10.4102/ajlm.v3i2.199. PMID: 27066396.

audits.title: Implementation of the World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa Stepwise Laboratory Quality Improvement Process Towards Accreditation.
audits.setting: 159 laboratories in WHO AFRO member states

cycle1.result: Mean score 69%; 70% achieved at least 2 stars (55% compliance) and 1% achieved 5 stars.

audits.other_findings: Internal audit and corrective action sections had mean scores below 50%.

audits.title: Creating a sustainable culture of quality through the SLMTA programme in a district hospital laboratory in Kenya.
audits.intervention: SLMTA workshops, mentorship, audits and integration of quality improvement into daily operations.

cycle2.result: Four stars (89%); three stars (81%) at external KENAS audit 12 months later.

audits.other_findings: EQA improved from 47% to 87%, sample rejection fell from 12% to 3%, and equipment repairs from 40 to 15 per year.
audits.citation: Maruti PM, Mulianga EA, Wambani LN, Wafula MN, Mambo FA, Mutisya SM, et al.. Creating a sustainable culture of quality through the SLMTA programme in a district hospital laboratory in Kenya. Afr J Lab Med. 2014;3(2):201. doi:10.4102/ajlm.v3i2.201. PMID: 29043184.

audits.title: From grass to grace: How SLMTA revolutionised the Bamenda Regional Hospital Laboratory in Cameroon.

cycle1.result: 18%, lowest in the cohort of five laboratories.

audits.intervention: SLMTA workshops, improvement projects and intensive on-site mentorship.

cycle2.result: 81% at official SLIPTA audit, highest in the cohort.

audits.other_findings: Improvement in all 12 Quality System Essentials, especially facilities and safety, and purchasing and inventory.
audits.citation: Nkwawir SC, Batumani NN, Maruta T, Awasom CN. From grass to grace: How SLMTA revolutionised the Bamenda Regional Hospital Laboratory in Cameroon. Afr J Lab Med. 2014;3(2):203. doi:10.4102/ajlm.v3i2.203. PMID: 29043186.

audits.title: Accelerating the spread of laboratory quality improvement efforts in Botswana.
audits.intervention: SLMTA workshops and improvement projects over nine months; four laboratories also had extra training and mentorship from the Botswana Bureau of Standards.
audits.other_findings: Laboratories with extra mentorship improved 21 points vs 8 points without.

audits.title: Translating a National Laboratory Strategic Plan into action through SLMTA in a district hospital laboratory in Botswana.
audits.intervention: SLMTA training, improvement projects, site visits and focused mentorship.

cycle2.result: 80% (three stars); 85% (four stars) at official audit nearly three years later.

audits.other_findings: Turnaround times fell 19% to 52%; patient satisfaction 56% to 73%; clinician satisfaction 41% to 72%.
audits.citation: Ntshambiwa K, Ntabe-Jagwer W, Kefilwe C, Samuel F, Moyo S. Translating a National Laboratory Strategic Plan into action through SLMTA in a district hospital laboratory in Botswana. Afr J Lab Med. 2014;3(2):209. doi:10.4102/ajlm.v3i2.209. PMID: 29043188.

audits.title: Implementation of the COVID-19 laboratory testing certification program (CoLTeP), Zimbabwe, 2021.
audits.standard: Checklist from ISO 15189:2012, ISO 15190:2020 and WHO Laboratory Safety Manual; certification at 90% or more

cycle1.result: 16 (62%) attained 5 stars and 10 (38%) 0-4 stars; test result and data management mean 93%

audits.other_findings: Weakest areas were biosafety and biosecurity (mean 73%) and quality control and assurance (mean 71%).
audits.citation: Chipendo T, Marembo T, Munemo C, Chituri H, Shumba E, Bangure D, et al.. Implementation of the COVID-19 laboratory testing certification program (CoLTeP), Zimbabwe, 2021. Pan Afr Med J. 2022;42:204. doi:10.11604/pamj.2022.42.204.34040. PMID: 36284574.
